In mathematics, the '''Sturm series'''<ref name="Sturm1829"/> associated with a pair of [[polynomial]]s is named after [[Jacques Charles François Sturm]].

==Definition==
{{See|Sturm chain}}
Let <math>p_0</math> and <math>p_1</math> two univariate polynomials. Suppose that they do not have a common root and the degree of <math>p_0</math> is greater than the degree of <math>p_1</math>. The ''Sturm series'' is constructed by:
:<math>
p_i := p_{i+1} q_{i+1} - p_{i+2} \text{ for } i \geq 0.
</math>
This is almost the same algorithm as [[Euclidean algorithm|Euclid's]] but the remainder <math>p_{i+2}</math> has negative sign.

==Sturm series associated to a characteristic polynomial==
Let us see now Sturm series <math>p_0,p_1,\dots,p_k</math> associated to a [[characteristic polynomial]] <math>P</math> in the variable <math>\lambda</math>:
:<math>
P(\lambda)= a_0 \lambda^k + a_1 \lambda^{k-1} + \cdots + a_{k-1} \lambda + a_k
</math>
where <math>a_i</math> for <math>i</math> in <math>\{1,\dots,k\}</math> are rational functions in <math>\mathbb{R}(Z)</math> with the coordinate set <math>Z</math>. The series begins with two polynomials obtained by dividing <math>P(\imath \mu)</math> by <math>\imath ^k</math> where <math>\imath</math> represents the imaginary unit equal to <math>\sqrt{-1}</math> and separate real and imaginary parts:
:<math>
\begin{align}
p_0(\mu) & := \Re \left(\frac{P(\imath \mu)}{\imath^k}\right ) = a_0 \mu^k - a_2 \mu^{k-2} + a_4 \mu^{k-4} \pm \cdots \\
p_1(\mu) & := -\Im \left( \frac{P(\imath \mu)}{\imath^k}\right)= a_1 \mu^{k-1} - a_3 \mu^{k-3} + a_5 \mu^{k-5} \pm \cdots
\end{align}
</math>

The remaining terms are defined with the above relation. Due to the special structure of these polynomials, they can be written in the form:
:<math>
p_i(\mu)= c_{i,0} \mu^{k-i} + c_{i,1} \mu^{k-i-2} + c_{i,2} \mu^{k-i-4}+\cdots
</math>
In these notations, the quotient <math>q_i</math> is equal to <math>(c_{i-1,0}/c_{i,0})\mu</math> which provides the condition <math>c_{i,0}\neq 0</math>. Moreover, the polynomial <math>p_i</math> replaced in the above relation gives the following recursive formulas for computation of the coefficients <math>c_{i,j}</math>.
:<math>
c_{i+1,j}= c_{i,j+1} \frac{c_{i-1,0}}{c_{i,0}}-c_{i-1,j+1} = \frac{1}{c_{i,0}} 
\det
\begin{pmatrix}
c_{i-1,0} & c_{i-1,j+1} \\
c_{i,0} & c_{i,j+1}
\end{pmatrix}.
</math>
If <math>c_{i,0}=0</math> for some <math>i</math>, the quotient <math>q_i</math> is a higher degree polynomial and the sequence <math>p_i</math> stops at <math>p_h</math> with <math>h<k</math>.
